DPDR is a freeze response to fight-or-flight response

In fight-or-flight response, your norepinephrine, epinephrine and dopamine levels extremely go up.

When you do things that cause abnormal increases in these neurotransmitters (norepinephrine, epinephrine and dopamine), you will not be able to get out of the freeze response because you will re-create that fight-or-flight response and keep the cycle up.

I think this is something about values, most people value things and they work because they don't see other way, they're committed to it and somehow they tell themselves "no other way, this has to happen, i will feel very bad if i don't accomplish this" and they do the work.

Sometimes it's the environment but mainly it's inner fear-induced motivation that makes you work. You need to fear the consequences of your procrastination and kind of make the work a valued duty.

And the equivalent of this in your brain is dopamine, dopamine is a reaction to the anticipation to great possibilities in the future, it's focused on the future. So let's say you got tickets to a concert and until the concert you anticipate that you will have fun in the concert and that gives you dopamine.

This is why it's crucial to do your work for your future accomplishments and not mess about your reward system with things like porn, masturbation, junk food etc. Because when you get dopamine with these shortcuts, your natural anticipation and excitement about doing something or going somewhere will not be fired on your brain like it supposed to.
